missionText: EEVL brings interactive experiments to students, teachers and researchers. Free tools, transparent models and a community that builds together.
buildWithUs: Build the next lab with us.
buildText: Bring your simulator, improve a translation, or help verify a model.
footer: An open project for electrical engineering education.
aboutIntro: Electrical Engineering Virtual Lab (EEVL) is a free, open-source educational portal for students, teachers, researchers and professionals. Explore. Simulate. Understand.
localText: Simulations run numerically on your device. There is no backend, account or API key. Previously accessed labs can work offline after all their resources have been cached.
scienceText: Models must explain their equations, assumptions, units, numerical methods and limitations. Being available in the catalog is not evidence of scientific validation.
experimentalText: Experimental: initial implementation without sufficient independent validation.
analyticText: Analytically verified: compared with a known analytical solution, with evidence.
numericText: Numerically validated: compared with an independent simulation tool, with evidence.
experimentText: Experimentally validated: compared with physical measurements, with evidence.
evidenceText: Validation levels require documented evidence. Imported applications remain experimental; the original circuit models have their own analytical verification reports. No experimental validation is claimed without measurements.
currentText: The catalog records the currently available applications, their actual languages and validation evidence. Portal descriptions can be translated independently from the applications. Circuit artwork is illustrative, not computed data.
privacyText: EEVL uses localStorage for language and theme, and Cache Storage for offline resources. No analytics or cookies are added. Clear site data in your browser to remove these preferences and cached files. Installation availability depends on your browser; use its install option when supported.
contributeTitle: Share what you know. Build what is next.
contributeIntro: Contributions from students, teachers and researchers are welcome. Start with a small, documented experiment and make it useful to the next person.
stepOneText: Copy templates/simulator into a new category directory and adjust relative paths. Reuse the existing model/UI separation and shared i18n. New applications must plan for pt-BR, en and es; list only the languages actually reviewed and available.
stepTwoText: Document equations, units, defaults, assumptions, numerical methods and limitations with a translation plan for Portuguese, English and Spanish. Compare analytical cases, test convergence and bounds, and cite references. Validation requires evidence.
stepThreeText: Add one entry to data/simulators.json with a unique ID, relative HTML path, thumbnail, translated title and description, keywords, category, difficulty, languages, authors, version, dates and validation evidence. New fields go in data/categories.json.
stepFourText: Run npm test and describe the model, changes and evidence in your pull request. Preserve existing authors and licenses. Contributions must remain compatible with static GitHub Pages hosting.
rcDescription: A worked example for contributors: charge an ideal capacitor through a resistor using a constant DC source.
templateNotice: Development template, not a catalog laboratory. The RC model has analytical comparison tests; it does not represent the Buck converter labs.
plotDescription: Computed capacitor voltage versus time. The dashed line shows the analytical solution. Numerical values are available in the results table or CSV.
invalidParameters: Invalid parameters. Use the ranges shown beside each input; use at most 100 time constants.
equationText: R · C · dvC/dt = Vs − vC. For a constant source: vC(t) = Vs + (vC(0) − Vs) · exp(−t/(R · C)). R in Ω, C in F, time in s and voltage in V. Ideal linear components, constant source and no loading or parasitic elements.
methodText: Classical fourth-order Runge–Kutta (RK4), uniform time step h ≤ R·C/50 and h ≤ duration/600. The model returns both numerical and exact solutions. At most 5002 samples; this bounded example does not need a Web Worker.
limitationsText: This first-order ideal model does not account for ESR, leakage, source resistance, switching, temperature or component tolerances. It is an educational calculation, not an electrical safety or hardware design assessment.
rcReferences: Derived from Kirchhoff’s voltage law and the ideal capacitor relation i = C·dv/dt. EEVL original contributor template · version 1.0.0 · MIT. Analytical comparison evidence and test commands: docs/VALIDATION.md.
tableText: The table shows 11 representative samples. Export CSV for all samples.
exportError: Export failed. Try exporting SVG instead.
queryError: The configuration URL contains invalid values. Default parameters were restored.
originalNotice: Original laboratory · original interface in Portuguese, with partial EN/ES presentation. The supplied model and interface are preserved. Scientific validation: experimental; no independent evidence has been supplied.

The iframe offers partial English/Spanish translation; the theme and numerical model are preserved. Full-page view keeps the translation.
authorUnspecified: Authorship not identified in supplied source

circuit_firstIntro: Charge, discharge and natural response of ideal RC and RL circuits driven by a DC source switched at \(t=0\). Compare the numerical RK4 solution with the closed form.
circuit_secondIntro: Series RLC driven by a voltage source and parallel RLC driven by a current source. Explore underdamped, critically damped and overdamped responses with a step-by-step derivation.
circuit_tabHint: Changing topology loads that circuit’s preset and recomputes the response.
circuit_signConvention: Passive sign convention. Series current circulates clockwise. Parallel branch currents point downward; voltage is measured at the common node.
circuit_preview: Plots show a uniform preview of at most 1800 points; the inspector, table and CSV use every integration sample. Results come from a local ideal-component model, not from measurements.
circuit_derivationIntro: Original derivation written for EEVL and typeset locally with KaTeX (LaTeX source below). Equations update with the selected topology.
circuit_method: The state equations are integrated with fixed-step classical Runge–Kutta (RK4). The step is \(h=T/N\), with \(N=\max(800,\lceil60Tr\rceil)\). \(T\) is the duration and \(r\) the fastest rate: \(1/\tau\) for first-order circuits, \(\alpha+\sqrt{\alpha^2-\omega_0^2}\) when overdamped, and \(\omega_0\) otherwise. Runs requiring more than 80000 steps are rejected instead of silently increasing the step. The closed-form solution is evaluated at the same instants and the maximum deviation is reported.
circuit_energyText: Stored energy is \(E=\tfrac12 C v_C^2+\tfrac12 L i_L^2\). The reported residual compares \(E(T)-E(0)\) with the trapezoidal integral of source power minus resistor loss.
circuit_limitations: Ideal linear \(R\), \(L\) and \(C\); ideal DC sources; no parasitics, saturation, tolerances or temperature effects. The source is constant for \(t\ge0\) and no pre-switch equilibrium is assumed, so the initial states are independent inputs. Series RLC accepts \(R=0\) (undamped). Parameter ranges are enforced; the model is a teaching tool and is not experimentally validated.
circuit_attribution: Derivations, code and tests are original EEVL contributions. Textbook references below are general background and do not endorse this implementation.
circuit_referenceNote: Verification level: analytically verified against closed-form solutions (see evidence). There is no experimental or SPICE validation.
circuit_chartDescription: Time-domain traces of the selected circuit quantities.
circuit_outOfRange: Some visible data is outside the plot range. Adjust the scale to see it.
circuit_dirty: Parameters changed. Run the simulation to update the results.
circuit_error_parameters: Invalid parameters. Check the ranges shown under each field.
circuit_error_resolution: This combination needs more than 80000 integration steps. Reduce the duration or the time-scale ratio; the step is never changed silently.
circuit_error_nonfinite: The computation produced a non-finite value and was discarded.
circuit_error_worker: The background worker could not run in this browser.
circuit_error_load: The page could not be initialized. Reload and try again.
circuit_voltageNote: Initial conditions are applied just after switching; the source stays constant during the simulation.
circuit_parallelNote: The parallel circuit is driven by a current source. At steady state, capacitor voltage is zero and inductor current equals source current.
circuit_rcKVL: Kirchhoff’s voltage law around the loop, with the resistor and capacitor relations.
circuit_substitute: Substituting the element relations gives a first-order linear ODE with an initial condition.
circuit_rcShift: Shift to the steady-state value and separate variables.
circuit_rcSolution: Closed-form capacitor voltage, time constant and resistor current.
circuit_zeroState: Zero-state transfer function and stored energy.
circuit_rlKVL: Kirchhoff’s voltage law around the loop, with the resistor and inductor relations.
circuit_rlShift: Shift to the steady-state current and separate variables.
circuit_rlSolution: Closed-form inductor current, time constant and inductor voltage.
circuit_seriesKVL: Kirchhoff’s voltage law for the series loop and the capacitor relation.
circuit_seriesStates: State-space form with states \(v_C\) and \(i_L\) (used by the RK4 integrator).
circuit_seriesODE: Eliminating \(i_L\) gives a second-order ODE for \(v_C\).
circuit_seriesShift: Shift by the forced value so the shifted equation is homogeneous; set the initial conditions.
circuit_seriesCoefficients: Natural frequency, damping coefficient, damping ratio and critical resistance.
circuit_parallelKCL: Kirchhoff’s current law at the top node with the element relations.
circuit_parallelStates: State-space form with states \(v\) and \(i_L\) (used by the RK4 integrator).
circuit_parallelODE: Differentiating the node equation (constant \(I_s\)) gives a homogeneous second-order ODE for \(v\).
circuit_parallelCoefficients: Natural frequency, damping coefficient, damping ratio and critical resistance.
circuit_characteristic: The characteristic roots determine the response regime.
circuit_seriesRecover: Recovering the circuit variables and the transfer function.
circuit_parallelRecover: Recovering the circuit variables and the impedance.
circuit_energyEquation: Energy stored and its rate of change (source power minus dissipation).
